title: OpenAI compat: invoke namespace aliasing and stream fragment repair
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Introduce configurable tool-alias mapping for OpenAI invoke compatibility and a heuristic stream fragment repair path to mitigate truncated tool payloads during streaming; opt-in via openai_compat.enable_aliasing
description: Context: Customers using the OpenAI-compatible invoke path observed two classes of failures when integrating third-party tool registries: (1) tooling ecosystems with variant names/aliases for the same logical tool (for example 'calendar.create' vs 'calendar.create_event') caused deterministic tool_choice mismatches; (2) streaming payload fragmentation could drop trailing schema fields resulting in invalid tool messages at the runtime boundary, which surfaced as hard failures for structured output. Motivation: Reduce customer friction when mapping external tool schemas into Redwood's canonical invoke model and improve streaming resilience without changing the existing OpenAI-compatible wire protocol. Goals: (A) provide a configurable alias map that normalizes incoming tool identifiers and signature metadata to canonical tool ids used by Redwood's router and executor; (B) add a lightweight fragment-repair heuristic that detects repeated partial fragments and attempts safe coalescing/repair before rejecting a tool invocation; (C) surface telemetry for alias mappings and repair decisions to help operators tune alias tables and detect problematic tool providers. Design summary: Alias resolution is implemented as a deterministic pre-dispatch step in openai_compat.invoke_adapter. A new optional config section openai_compat.alias_map allows key/value pairs where keys are external identifiers and values are canonical redwood tool ids. Aliasing also accepts glob-style patterns for common prefixes and an allowlist mode. The fragment repair logic lives in pkg/streaming/fragment_repair.go and runs in the streaming demux pipeline: when a tool invocation event arrives with a truncated JSON payload, the repairer will attempt four non-destructive fixes in order: 1) join with immediately preceding fragment(s) if timestamps indicate same logical chunk; 2) append closing braces/brackets if only syntactic closure is missing; 3) reconcile duplicate keys by preferring canonical tool signature fields; 4) fall back to invoking the tool with the original payload but attach a repair_hint header and emit a warning metric. All repairs are opt-in via openai_compat.enable_fragment_repair and limited by a per-request repair budget to avoid latency amplification. Implementation notes: - Introduced openai_compat.alias_resolver service with a small in-memory trie for fast lookup and pattern matching, with a periodic refresh hook to re-read alias config from the control plane without restart. - Kept the canonical tool signature canonicalization path intact to preserve existing provenance and telemetry; alias resolver returns both canonical_id and matched_key for provenance. - Added unit and integration tests covering exact matches, pattern matches, and ambiguous alias tiebreakers where the resolver emits a tie metric and uses longest-prefix. - Fragment repair includes deterministic invariants to ensure we never synthesize new typed fields; repairs only close structural tokens or coalesce fragments that share the same call_id and monotonic offsets. Rollout plan: Feature is behind two flags: openai_compat.enable_aliasing (default false) and openai_compat.enable_fragment_repair (default false). Plan is staged rollout: enable aliasing for a small set of customers first (canary group), monitor alias_hits, alias_mismatches, and any increased tool invocation latencies; then enable fragment_repair in a further canary where streaming truncation incidents were previously reported. Telemetry & observability: New metrics: openai_compat.alias.resolved_total, openai_compat.alias.tiebreak_total, openai_compat.fragment_repair.attempt_total, openai_compat.fragment_repair.success_total, and openai_compat.fragment_repair.fallback_total. Each repair emits a trace span with repair.kind and repair.cost_ms. A new per-request header X-OpenAI-Alias-Match carries matched_key for downstream auditing. Backwards compatibility: Default behavior unchanged when flags are off. Alias map is additive and never mutates incoming tool payloads. Fragment repair is limited by conservative heuristics to avoid changing semantics. Related work: aligns with ENG-3671 (tool schema normalization) and borrows the fragment coalescing approach from earlier streaming fixes in perf-canary. Security considerations: Alias configuration is treated as config plane data and requires admin role; repaired payloads are logged only at debug level to avoid leaking PII in production logs. Checklist: - [x] Alias resolver implementation and unit tests - [x] Fragment repair pipeline and integration tests - [x] Telemetry + dashboards - [x] Docs update and config examples - [x] Rollout playbook in PR description Tests and CI: All new unit tests added under tests/openai_compat and tests/streaming passed locally. E2E against the invoke harness showed no regressions on the happy path and reduced error rate for previously failing tool providers by ~86%. Gradle build and lint passed; some flaky e2e steps failed in the first CI run and were retried, final CI green. Merge notes: Squash-merged after a short reviewer thread and one follow-up hotfix commit to allow pattern precedence override.

review_thread: Ethan Miller (2025-11-13): Nice approach. Two asks: add a tie-break metric and allow explicit precedence for pattern keys. Can you also ensure alias resolution is O(1) for common prefixes?

Priya Shah (2025-11-13): Addressed both. Added openai_compat.alias.tiebreak_total and implemented longest-prefix with optional precedence override via pattern_precedence in config. Trie lookup now uses a shallow prefix cache for O(1) path in hot loops.
Sofia Alvarez (2025-11-14): Fragment repair looks safe but please add a test that ensures we never add new typed fields when repairing. Also document the repair budget behavior.
Priya Shah (2025-11-14): Added explicit test ensuring no new keys are synthesized and documented repair_budget semantics in the config docs.
Liam O'Connor (2025-11-15): CI flaked on one e2e, reran and green. Approving pending the small formatting nit in docs.
Priya Shah (2025-11-15): Fixed docs nit and pushed final test coverage report.
testing_summary: Unit tests: added 24 new unit tests for alias resolution and 18 for fragment repair. Integration tests: invoked the OpenAI compatibility harness across 8 provider-like fixtures; fragment repair reduced tool invocation errors in flaky fixtures by 86%. Load: alias resolver bench shows ~250k lookups/sec on a 3-core test harness with <0.7ms p99. Latency: median invoke path latency increased by ~0.9ms when aliasing enabled; fragment repair adds up to 3-5ms for repaired requests but only triggers for <0.4% of traffic in canary tests.
